content: Current trial uses the wrist camera and an external third-person camera. The operator repositioned the external camera on 2026-09-26 before this run. Re-establish the external viewpoint from fresh images; do not reuse old external pixel directions, camera extrinsics, or apparent gaps from previous runs. The camera may move again: distinguish camera motion from robot motion using joint feedback and fresh scene context. Use both fresh views on every decision, but give the third-person/top view primary authority over coarse distance, approach progress, height, and clearance. Use the wrist view primarily for lateral centering and, only during the final approach, for ball depth between the fingers. Perspective in the wrist view can make a still-distant ball look large: if the top view still shows visible physical separation between the gripper/finger roots and the ball, classify the task as coarse approach even when the ball is large and centered in the wrist image. Historical images establish opening direction and a pre-grasp appearance only; they do not establish present clearance.

content:
Use the original GPT-Policy Cartesian workflow. Choose absolute TCP targets and orientations from fresh dual-camera observations, measured joints, command joints, and previous results. There is no task-level fixed Cartesian step size. Choose the travel distance and number of waypoints according to visible clearance, confidence in the direction, proximity to contact, and host motion limits. Prefer move_eef_chunk for a clear contact-free path that does not need intermediate observation. move_to and move_eef_chunk already run the host IK, joint-limit, path-budget and timing checks before dispatch; a separate check_path is optional for uncertain reachability or comparing alternatives, not mandatory before every action. A successful numeric check is not proof of collision clearance or physical arrival. Observe again at contact, gripper changes, occlusion, tracking anomalies, or when direction is uncertain.
Use the top/external view as the primary coarse-approach distance and clearance reference; the wrist view checks whether the ball is in the open-finger corridor and confirms final insertion depth. Wrist centering or apparent size alone does not mean the ball is within reach. Choose forward, lateral, vertical and orientation changes as supported by the current views and observed response; do not hard-code repeated base +X motion or a fixed sequence of axes. Previous local response evidence (+X appeared to approach, -Y shifted the ball left) is historical and must be reassessed after posture or camera changes. demonstrated_pregrasp_guide is an optional IK/posture reference, not a required waypoint or a sequence to replay.
Inspect J1..J6 actual motion, command residuals, limit margins and visual progress after execution. The planner starts from tcp_command_xyzquat to preserve command continuity. When constructing an incremental target, use that complete commanded pose as the reference; do not splice measured XYZ with the commanded orientation and call it a pure translation. Measured TCP remains essential evidence of actual progress and residuals, but it is not an automatic command re-anchor. Only a host-reported re-anchor establishes a new command reference. Do not claim a nonmoving joint recovered merely because its target was reset. During clear contact-free coarse approach, do not call give_up solely because one host-accepted action has a small FK discrepancy, a bounded joint residual, or a joint with little measured change. Compare net measured and dual-view approach progress across the last three distinct approach actions when available, considering the requested joint changes. Unchanged-target holds and observation-only turns do not count as independent movement attempts. If useful progress and clearance remain, continue with a supported approach or correction; exact TCP arrival and zero residual are not prerequisites. A single tiny opposite-sign FK change is inconclusive, not proof that the whole approach is unsafe. Do not label a discrepancy as random noise without evidence. If progress is absent, consider a meaningfully different supported correction rather than repeatedly holding or accumulating the same ineffective command. Host faults, stale feedback, visible obstruction/contact risk, or clear unintended motion require immediate stopping without waiting for a trend window. Persistent growing residuals together with no useful progress and no supported safe alternative still require handoff. Do not bypass host limits, hide errors by resetting targets, or infer contact from a stall.
Host motion budgets apply per attended segment. If check_path or execution explicitly requires session renewal, end this blocked segment with a precise reason for the host; do not spend repeated decisions checking the same locked target or try smaller steps to bypass the lock. The model cannot reset budgets itself. Keep the gripper open during approach. Close separately and incrementally only when both views support that the ball has reached the grasp region near the finger roots, respecting gripper_step_limit_normalized. Report grasp success only with fresh evidence of retention or operator confirmation; closure or stall alone is not proof.

Current operator feedback: wrist-image alignment has overestimated grasp readiness while the external/global view still shows a height or approach gap. Prioritize the fresh external/top view for vertical alignment, remaining approach distance, and actual finger-to-ball placement throughout the task, including final alignment and closure. Use the wrist view for lateral centering and insertion detail only when consistent with external evidence. A ball projected between the fingers or near their roots in the wrist image is not sufficient for closure. If the external view shows the fingers above/beside the ball or still separated, do not close further or lift; first correct the approach pose from fresh visual response and joint feedback. If partly closed while misaligned, reopen enough to restore clearance before correcting position. Do not assume an occluded contact region is touching, or infer metric distances from uncalibrated pixels. Before closing or lifting, explain the external-view evidence in the action note. Success requires the ball visibly leaving the table and remaining held; image overlap or closure alone is not success.
